hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge 3 with a skip adds a direct input-to-output path, whereas replacing an existing op gives little or negative gain.
Activating a dead direct edge to the output with a conv adds capacity and connectivity.
With the direct 0->3 edge absent, removing edge 0 can cut off the input from the output.
Without the direct edge 3, the output depends more on edge 5, so removing it hurts.
When edge 1 is absent, a skip on edge 2 restores a usable input-to-output route via node 2.
Deleting an existing 3x3 conv removes learned capacity, unlike deleting weaker ops on parallel paths.
A conv on edge 2 is only useful if edge 0 feeds it, so cutting edge 0 hurts more.
Turning a dead edge into a conv adds a path and capacity, which is rarely the case when replacing an existing op.
Adding a skip to an absent edge creates a connection, while swapping out an existing conv loses capacity.
With edge 1 absent, edge 4 is a main route into node 3, so strengthening it matters more.
